subject: Dedicated capacity: StrataTek burst governance & slab sizing
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratatek.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stratatek.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for May launch — burst & autoscale options

Kimberly / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We confirmed an internal go/no-go for a staged product launch starting the week of May 24 and I wanted to surface capacity expectations so we can converge on a Dedicated sizing + burst plan. High level numbers from our traffic model:
- Baseline steady-state traffic: ~120 reqs/min for the primary endpoint (avg 1.2s generation).
- Expected peak windows: 3x baseline for 2x daily 20–30 minute windows (marketing-driven spikes), and a launch-day spike estimate up to ~12x baseline for a 60–90 minute window.
- Workload mix: 70% low-latency interactive, 30% batch (async embeddings and reranks).

Ask: can you propose a Dedicated slab + burst arrangement that gives us predictable baseline throughput but also covers the launch spike without a multi-hour cold failure? We're interested in options that balance committed baseline (to lower unit cost) and burst guardrails (credits, prewarm, autoscale thresholds). Also want to understand eviction behavior and any SLA/ops implications.

I've attached our launch plan (stratatek-launch-plan.pdf). Procurement copied here — they'll want the commercial headroom numbers and contract language.

Appreciate a short runbook-style recommendation and any quick follow-ups for pricing. Can we get a proposal by EOD Apr 28 PST?

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Infrastructure, StrataTek
alex.morgan@stratatek.com
stratatek.com

Attachment: stratatek-launch-plan.pdf

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratatek.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-28T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for May launch — burst & autoscale options

Alex — thanks for the clear numbers and the plan. Below is an initial proposal (high level) so we can align internally and get pricing to Procurement. I kept it pragmatic to avoid over-committing ahead of the final load test.

Proposal (initial):
- Reserved slab: 6 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (baseline commit) sized for the 70% interactive mix.
- Ephemeral burst pool: additional 4 x A100-80GB GPUs accessible during burst windows (soft-evictable).
- Headroom: target 40% headroom above baseline for short windows (up to 30 mins) via autoscale + prewarm. For launch-day 12x spike we expect the ephemeral pool to absorb the first 45–60 min; after that we fall back to queued rate-limited behavior unless we trigger emergency on-demand capacity.
- Autoscale policy (summary):
  - Scale-up trigger: if 90th percentile queue wait > 200ms for 2 continuous minutes OR backend CPU/GPU utilization > 85% for sustained 60s
  - Prewarm: keep 1 prewarmed instance per 2 GPUs in the slab ready during expected marketing windows (configurable)
  - Scale-down: gentle cooldown (5–10 minute window) with a prefer-evict-to-soft-preempt ordering
- Eviction order (soft eviction): preemptible batch jobs -> opportunistic prewarm -> interactive best-effort instances. We avoid evicting pinned customer interactive sessions unless explicit emergency fallback is accepted.
- Burst credit model: we can offer 600 burst GPU-hours/month and overage at our on-demand rate. Credits are consumed only for ephemeral pool hours; reserved slab hours are billed per commit.

I've attached a starter spreadsheet (redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1.xlsx) with baseline RPS -> GPU mapping and an ops playbook excerpt. Ben and Karthik — please review the autoscale numbers and commercial assumptions below and call out any changes.

Next steps: internal alignment today; commercial proposal to Procurement by Apr 29 morning. Also propose a 30-min alignment call tomorrow to walk the runbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1.xlsx

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratatek.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-29T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for May launch — burst & autoscale options

Kimberly / Alex — quick technical notes from the serving/runtime side. I quoted Kimberly's baseline and added a few operational guardrails.

Notes:
- Sizing rationale: with the model variants you described and typical token lengths, 1 A100-80GB equiv handles ~20–25 sustained interactive QPS with our continuous-batching pipeline. That maps the proposed 6 GPUs to roughly 120–150 steady-state QPS, which matches your baseline.
- Burst absorption: ephemeral 4 GPUs give us ~80–100 QPS of additional interactive capacity. Combined with 40% headroom and prewarm, we should absorb the marketing spikes (3x) comfortably. The launch-day 12x spike will exceed ephemeral capacity; to reduce customer-visible failures we recommend applying request-level throttling and prioritized queuing during the tail of the surge.
- Prewarm behaviour: prewarm instances keep model weights loaded and KV cache warm — they cut cold-starts from ~6s down to ~200–400ms for warm requests. We should define prewarm windows in the contract to avoid undue cost.
- Autoscale specifics to codify in ops:
  * Warm-up policy: add one ephemeral instance per 10% sustained increase above baseline, with a 45s ramp throttle.
  * Eviction signal: use cluster reclaim with 60s grace to finish in-flight tokens; if timeouts occur, automatic retry with exponential backoff at client-side is required.
- Efficiency suggestion: if StrataTek can accept an int8 quantized model variant for some routes (especially batch embeddings/rerank), we can reduce GPU-hours for those routes by ~30% and make the ephemeral pool stretch further. We'll need a validation run to ensure quality parity.

I've attached a short snippet with autoscale policy examples and the prewarm cost heuristics (autoscale-policies-snippet.txt).

Happy to jump on the call and walk through a simulated spike and expected tail latency.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: autoscale-policies-snippet.txt

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratatek.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-29T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for May launch — burst & autoscale options

Thanks — commercial framing from my side. Key bullets for Procurement and deal terms:

Commercials (draft):
- Baseline commit: 6 GPUs equivalent — list price $26,400/month (example; final T&Cs in SOW).
- Burst credits: 600 GPU-hours/month included. Overage: $28/GPU-hour for ephemeral usage beyond credits.
- Discount option: 12-month commit reduces baseline to $22,000/month and increases included burst credits to 900 GPU-hours/month.
- Prewarm add-on: prewarm reservation charged as fractional GPU-hours (we'll show line items in the SOW).
- SLA and support: 99.9% availability on reserved slab; ephemeral pool best-effort during surge events. For launch-day emergency capacity we can open an ops escalation channel and trigger prioritized provisioning in a second region if requested (subject to cross-region data policy and latency impact).

Deal mechanics: include HubSpot link and we'll attach the SOW + pricing worksheet for Procurement. If StrataTek wants a fallback to EU region for spillover, that requires an addendum for data residency and network egress.

I'll draft a clean proposal and DocuSign package if Alex confirms the baseline size. Draft HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-4821-ST

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratatek.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@stratatek.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for May launch — burst & autoscale options

Appreciate the detailed breakdown — this is helpful. A few clarifications from Product and Procurement:
- Eviction notice window: Procurement wants to avoid any customer-visible termination without 5m advance notice where possible. Can you confirm the 60s reclaim + retries behaviour and whether we can expose a 5-minute grace window for our interactive routes?
- Cross-region fallback: We want an option to spill to EU for emergency capacity; please outline latency impact (approx +60–120ms) and any data residency addendum.
- Can you provide the SOW template and a clean price sheet with both 12-mo and 36-mo options?

Procurement attached their vendor terms template (procurement-template-stratatek.docx) — procurement@stratatek.com will coordinate redlines.

Also, we'd like a short 30-min call to finalize the baseline and sign off on SOW. We're available Apr 30 afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Alex

Attachment: procurement-template-stratatek.docx

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratatek.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-30T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for May launch — burst & autoscale options

Alex — thanks, understood. Quick answers and next steps:
- Eviction / grace: we can document a 5-minute app-level grace period for pinned interactive routes in the SOW. Operationally, the cluster reclaim remains a hard 60s reclaim signal, but our agents will attempt session handoff and retries for up to 5 minutes before dropping. We'll codify retry behavior in the runbook and include a note for client-side backoff.
- Cross-region fallback: we can enable EU spillover for emergency provisioning. Expect additional latency of ~80–120ms depending on egress. We'll prepare an addendum for data residency and outline cost implications.
- Deliverables by EOD Apr 30 PST: updated SOW + pricing (12- and 36-month options), a one-page runbook excerpt, and a revised capacity matrix (capacity-matrix-v2.xlsx).

I'll schedule a 30-min alignment at 4:00pm PST today and include the draft SOW for review. If Procurement prefers an alternate time, let me know.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: capacity-matrix-v2.xlsx
